acme-admin: Hey, hitting an odd OAuth callback failure for our mobile deeplink flow. After redirect back from GitHub we get a `400 state_mismatch` and the callback path appears to have a stray semicolon in the query string. Happens intermittently on iOS Safari, Android Chrome seems fine.
Maya Patel: Thanks — can you paste the exact redirect URL you see in the browser when it fails?
acme-admin: Sure — here's an example captured from the device console: `https://app.example.com/callback;?code=xyz&state=abc123&session=def` — note the `;` before the `?`. When that happens our handler treats the path as `/callback;` and cookie path does not match so PKCE state is missing from session cookie.
Alex R.: Interesting. Do you use any redirect normalization in your reverse proxy or CDN? Sometimes edge strips or rewrites `;` differently.
acme-admin: We have CloudFront + a small Fastly-like proxy. No explicit normalization rules that I know of. It only seems to happen when users click a deeplink that has an encoded semicolon earlier in the flow. If we URL-encode the semicolon (`%3B`) before handing to GitHub the callback is fine.
Sam O.: Can you repro reliably with a curl or an automated script? If so, include request/response headers and the Set-Cookie on the original auth start and the cookie on the callback.
acme-admin: I put together a short repro:
```
# start auth
GET https://auth.example.com/start?redirect_uri=myapp://open;callback%3Ffoo=1
# GitHub returns to
https://app.example.com/callback;?code=xyz&state=abc123
```
When the callback arrives with that `;` we see `Set-Cookie: session=...; Path=/` earlier, but the browser stores cookie for `/callback` and not `/callback;` so server can't find the session.
Maya Patel: Thanks, that helps a lot. Two quick asks: 1) can you grep your proxy logs for the raw request line to see if the `;` arrives to the origin or is introduced by the client? 2) try passing the redirect_uri to GitHub with semicolon percent-encoded (`%3B`) as a temporary workaround.
acme-admin: Grepped the proxy logs — shows the `;` present in the incoming request line before it hits our origin. `%3B` variant doesn't reproduce.
Alex R.: Ok, that means the deeplink or app is sending an actual `;` (or the mobile/webview is converting). Two mitigation paths: enforce normalization on the proxy to strip `;` from the path before matching cookie scope, or update our callback handler to normalize path before looking up session cookie. Both have tradeoffs.
Sam O.: We can try a quick fix: normalize request URL by stripping trailing semicolons and collapsing `;?` to `?` at the proxy edge. I'll push a canary rule to the staging edge and ask acme-admin to test.
Support Bot: deploy-canary succeeded for edge/normalize-semicolon-rule (canary id: c-2026-03-17-01).
acme-admin: Tested staging canary — callback now lands at `https://app.example.com/callback?code=xyz&state=abc123` and auth completes. No more state_mismatch.
Maya Patel: Great. We'll schedule a rollout to prod with a rollback window and add an alert if we see 5xx spike. Also filing a follow-up to update our deeplink docs recommending percent-encoding reserved chars: https://redwood.internal/docs/deeplinks#encode-reserved-chars
acme-admin: Thanks everyone — appreciate the fast turnaround. We'll keep an eye and report if any other clients still hit it. :raised_hands:
__note: Single Slack thread string in 'text'. Messages are chronological and prefixed with sender. Metadata fields required by agents.md present.
